Foiling is a pricing tier, not a cosmetic detail

Flesh and Blood separates its printings by foiling as much as by rarity. Cold foil and rainbow foil versions of a card trade well above the non-foil run, and on sought-after cards the gap is large.

Card AI suggests the matching card record with set, card number and available rarity data. Confirm cold foil, rainbow foil or non-foil in Review before pricing or saving it.

Legendary, Fabled and Majestic sit on their own curves

The rarity ladder in Flesh and Blood maps closely onto price, and the upper tiers are thinly traded. Recording rarity per card keeps those positions visible in a collection instead of averaged away.

First edition and unlimited printings

Where a card exists in both first edition and unlimited runs, the two trade separately. Edition is part of the card record, so each is stored and valued as its own entry.

Flesh and Blood card scanner questions.

Can the scanner tell cold foil from rainbow foil?

The scan suggests the card record, but you confirm cold foil, rainbow foil or non-foil in Review. Each confirmed finish is stored and priced separately.

Does Card AI track first edition Flesh and Blood cards separately?

Yes. Edition is stored per card, so first edition and unlimited copies are separate entries in your collection.

What is my Flesh and Blood card worth?

Select the matching catalog record, confirm the finish, and choose a raw condition or existing slab grade. Card AI then shows the relevant market price.

Is there a way to check values without scanning?

Yes. Look up flesh and blood card value by name, set or rarity from the card database, and the cards you own form a flesh and blood collection tracker with a live total.
